faq.q: What time does the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise depart?
faq.a: The cruise departs Puerto Banús at 10:00 and returns by 13:00, giving you a full three-hour morning on the sea. We recommend arriving 15 minutes early to board and settle in.

faq.q: Which boats are available for the dolphin watching brunch cruise?
faq.a: The standard option is our Tier A fleet: the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax). Both are comfortable motor yachts with sun pads, a shaded cockpit, and a small galley for serving brunch.

We cannot guarantee sightings as dolphins are wild animals, but the Bay of Marbella is a known feeding ground for striped dolphins (Stenella coeruleoalba). Sightings occur on roughly 80% of morning cruises between April and October.

faq.q: What food and drink is included in the brunch?
faq.a: The charter includes water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks (e.g., olives, crisps, nuts, fresh fruit). For a fuller brunch, you can order a catered platter (€25/person, payable on board) – please let us know 48 hours in advance.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food or drink?
faq.a: Yes, you are welcome to bring your own food and non-alcoholic drinks. However, the skipper reserves the right to limit alcohol consumption for safety. The boat has a small fridge and cooler box.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
faq.a: In case of adverse weather (high winds, rough seas, or storms), the skipper may cancel or reschedule the cruise. You will receive a full refund or the option to move to a later date, with no extra charge.

faq.q: Is the cruise suitable for children?
faq.a: Yes, the cruise is family-friendly. Children are welcome on board, and life jackets are available in all sizes. The boat has a shaded area for sun protection. Children under 3 go free.

faq.q: How do I book the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise?
faq.a: You can book directly through our website or contact us via WhatsApp. A 50% deposit is required to secure the date, with the balance due 7 days before departure.

data.body_html:
Start your morning with a Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2036 – a three-hour charter from Puerto Banús that combines wild dolphin sightings with cava, snacks, and the Mediterranean breeze. Departing at 10:00, you'll cruise the Bay of Marbella aboard a private motor yacht, skipper included, with all drinks and light bites provided. Prices start at €749 for two hours on our Tier A boats – the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 – making this one of the most affordable boat hire Marbella experiences for families and small groups.

What to expect on your dolphin watching brunch cruise

After boarding at Puerto Banús, your skipper will head west towards the Cabopino coastline, where striped dolphins (Stenella coeruleoalba) are frequently spotted feeding in the nutrient-rich waters. The boat slows down as dolphins approach, giving you clear views from the bow or the sun pads. While sightings aren't guaranteed, the morning light and calm sea make for excellent photo opportunities. The brunch service begins once you're underway – expect cava, white wine, beer, soft drinks, and a selection of light snacks (olives, crisps, nuts, fresh fruit). For a heartier meal, you can pre-order a catered platter (€25/person) with cured meats, cheese, bread, and pastries.

Which boat is right for your group?

The standard dolphin watching brunch cruise uses our Tier A fleet:

  • Astondoa 40 – 12.5m, 9 passengers, sun pads, shaded cockpit, small galley
  • Azimut 39 – 12.5m, 11 passengers, spacious flybridge, wet bar, bow sunbeds

Both boats depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and 21% IVA. The €749 price covers 2 hours; you can extend to 3 hours (€1,049) or a full day (8 hours, €2,299) if you'd like to combine dolphin watching with a longer cruise to Estepona or Sotogrande. For larger groups (up to 12 guests), consider our Azimut 58 Flybridge or the Mangusta 80 – pricing on request via WhatsApp.

Best time of year for dolphin watching in Marbella

Striped dolphins are resident year-round in the Alboran Sea, but the highest sighting rates occur between April and October, when water temperatures range from 16°C to 24°C. Morning cruises (10:00–13:00) benefit from calm seas and low wind, especially in summer when the afternoon Levante wind picks up. Winter cruises (November–March) are cooler but often more reliable for dolphin activity, as the dolphins follow baitfish closer to shore. On any given morning, the skipper will use local knowledge to find the best spots – typically 2–5 nautical miles off the coast between Marbella Marina and Cabopino.

What's included in the price – and what's extra

Every charter includes: licensed skipper, fuel, water + soft drinks + beer + white wine + cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). What's not included:

  • Catered brunch platter (€25/person, must be ordered 48 hours in advance)
  • Private chef or waiter (available on request, €150 extra)
  • Special dietary requests (gluten-free, vegan – please advise at booking)
  • Gratuities for the skipper (optional, 10–15% of charter price is customary)

If you're celebrating a birthday or anniversary, we can arrange a cake (€40) or a bottle of Champagne (€60). Just let us know when you book.

How to book your Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2036

Booking is straightforward – choose your preferred date and boat on our website, pay a 50% deposit, and we'll confirm within 24 hours. The balance is due 7 days before departure. All bookings include free cancellation up to 48 hours before the cruise. For same-day bookings, please contact us via WhatsApp to check availability. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance during July and August, when demand is highest. For more ideas on how to spend your day on the water, browse our full range of Marbella boat charters.
